properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Huntley & Huntley Inc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-02-10
Violation Code: 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
Violation ID: 877013
Permit API: 003-21903
Unconventional: No
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Frazer Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-02-10
Comments: This inspection is being conducted as follow up to inspection 2975835 in which violations were issued for the well not being properly labeled. WQS Trainee Andrew Zadzilko is assisting. Conditions on site are rainy and approximately 47 degrees. There appears to be several erosion channels on the access road which are leading to low spots in the access road causing stormwater to pool at those locations. One (Photo 1-4) appears to be discharging sediment laden water into a roadside ditch. Another spot along the access road (Photo 7) is discharging into a culvert which is in turn discharging it into a well vegetated area. The Department recommends that the operator remediate the discharge (Photo 1-4) immediately and maintain the access road in a condition that will prevent future erosion and sedimentation issues. The operator was contacted by the Department in regard to this discharge. The Operator advised that due to weather issues no work had been conducted to address accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues on the access road network. There appears to be a bare spot adjacent to the well site (Photo 11) which is collecting stormwater and discharging it into a well vegetated area. The Department is requesting more information on how this bare spot was formed. The Department also recommends that the operator permanently stabilize this area to prevent storm water from creating accelerated erosion channels or possible impacting WOTC. The site appears constructed and equipped for production. The well is labeled. There are no leaks, dead or distressed vegetation observed. Based on this inspection the violation for the well label will be closed as corrected. Additional violations are being issued for the accelerated erosion to the access road and discharge of sediment laden water to WOTC. Additional violations may be issued based on responses from the operator.

Inspection Date: 2019-04-10
Comments: This inspection was performed in response to the report of a small release of production fluid along Irvine Run, in Brokenstraw Township, Warren County, PA. Rick Engelbert, with Irvine Run Resources, contacted the Department to report a broken pipeline which resulted in the release of approximately ½ of a barrel of crude oil, to the ground along Irvine Run. Unconventional: No

Municipality: Somerset Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/12/2023
Comments: On December 12 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the Cole 1 OG Well in response to IR 3641696.The findings are as follows: The area of a leak around the production tank previously observed appeared to have undergone remediation activities. It appeared impacted soil had been removed and filled in with a fine, light colored material. This fine, light colored material appeared to be holding an excess amount of water resulting in the ground surrounding the production tank to be soft and not properly stabilized. The Department attempted to take conductivity readings of the soil but was unable to dig below the newly placed material as it was so saturated it filled any holes dug back in. Conductivity readings of new material were taken with readings of 0.23mS and 0.35mS. Prior to leaving the location, the Department contacted KPI Representative Joel Greco to inquire about the remediation efforts and saturated material around the production tank resulting in improper stabilization. Mr.Greco stated they remediated the site by removing almost 3 tons of impacted material. This material is now being stored off site, awaiting sampling to determine how to dispose of it. He also stated that the fine, light color material is a fine limestone material that was placed in the area of excavation. He insured that the material would stabilize after it dries once, allowing it to compact. Based on today's inspection, violations associated with the spill remain open as the remediation efforts are still being reviewed by the Department. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending a follow up inspection.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BEECH RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 9/26/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8202740
Permit API: 081-21954
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Lycoming Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/26/2024
Comments: On September 26, 2024, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a routine site inspection at the Beech Resources Delta Well Pad. No E and S issues were observed during the time of inspection. The site appeared to be stable and well vegetated meeting the 70% uniform perennial vegetative cover.Beech Resources contractors were in the process of setting up the well pad with production equipment and working on getting the AST ready for use. During the inspection, the east end of the well pad had some pools of water on it. The DEP screened the pool of water at the northeast corner with a conductivity meter. The conductivity meter measured the conductivity of the pool of water at 6,000 uS/cm. Near the pool of water in the northeast corner was a frack tank outside of containment. This frack tank contained water from the secondary containment of the drilling rig. Adjacent to the frack tank were multiple pallets of hoses used to manifold tanks together. The conductivity of the pool of water near and under the frack tank measured at 13,090 uS/cm. After observing the pools of water with elevated conductivity, the DEP went to the Company Man onsite and informed him of the findings. DEP showed the company where the pool of water was and the Company Man said that Beech Resources Don Stevenson was onsite. After finding Mr. Stevenson, DEP showed where the elevated conductivity pool was. Mr. Stevenson placed a call for a vac truck to mobilize to the well pad to removed the fluid. An excavator was used to dig a sump to collect the fluid so the vac truck could remove the fluid. Once the vac truck arrived onsite, Beech resources began removing the fluid from the sump and around the frack tank. The pallets of hoses were moved onto containment. During the removal of the fluid from the northeast corner conductivity was monitored in the fluid of the sump. Prior to DEP leaving the site, conductivity of the fluid in the sump measured at 3,900 uS/cm. Conductivity of the fluid was higher near the frack tank in the sump that was dug.At 1630 on September 26, 2024, Mr. Stevenson called DEP to inform them that all the fluid had been vacuumed and impacted soil had been removed. Mr. Stevenson said they were able to move the frack tank onto containment. After moving the frack tank, excavation of the impacted soil could begin. Mr. Stevenson said they removed approximately an excavator's bucket width for about 25 feet and removed about 6 inches of soil. Approximately 32 gallons of fluid was vacuumed and two roll off dumpsters were filled with impacted soil.Due to the amount of soil removed combined with the fluid vacuumed up Beech Resources has chosen to remediate to Act 2 standards. Violations of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.66(b)1, Chapter 78a.57(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301 were noted.

Distressed vegetation was observed in areas on the fill slopes (photos #5 and 7) and downslope of the constructed "corner" berm (photo #4). A representative with Repsol walked us up to the 7H wellhead. Fluids were observed within the well cellar. Comments: WQS Gene Rickard and I performed an INCDT inspection of the Mitchell well site regarding a reported release which occurred aroung 0830 on Jan. 30, 2019. The complaint number was 339494. The release was reported to me via Briana Cunningham, WQSS. Other individuals on site were Mike Deming and Mr. Otten of Southwestern Energy Production Co. The weather at the time of inspection was around 15 degrees F and snowing. Wind was gusting. At about 0830 hrs. a tank in the onsite tank battery was being filled from a production fluid tank. The operator allegedly was monitoring the tank level from the hatch nearest the front part of the tank. According to a relayed assessment, the operator thought the tank was positioned not quite level, allowing the fluid level to overflow the back part of the tank, spilling onto the containment area surrounding the battery. The containment was later found to be compromised and allowed water to leave the containment area. SWN notified the Department on 1/30/2019. According to onsite representatives, approximately 5-6 bbls. of produced water were released to containment, then through the compromised liner to the pad surface. Resource Environmental was called in to delineate the impacted area, and has been directing a dewatering action to mitigate the impact until the tank battery can be moved, as the tanks are currently frozen to the ground. The timeframe for moving the tanks to delineate the affected area appears to be over the weekend. While onsite, crews were attempting to locate any tears in containment, which was being hampered by the icy buildup inside the containment. Workers were also mobilizing tankers to dewater the area and tanks in the tank battery in preparation for movement off containment to allow resource to delineate the affected area. The affected area seems to stop about 10' from the berm, according to test pits dug for assessment. The spill will be going to Act 2. SWN Representative Mike Deming said a possible change in protocol from a 6" to a 12" tank freeboard is being considered. Violations are attached.

According to a relayed assessment, the operator thought the tank was positioned not quite level, allowing the fluid level to overflow the back part of the tank, spilling onto the containment area surrounding the battery. The containment was later found to be compromised and allowed water to leave the containment area. SWN notified the Department on 1/30/2019. According to onsite representatives, approximately 5-6 bbls. of produced water were released to containment, then through the compromised liner to the pad surface. Resource Environmental was called in to delineate the impacted area, and has been directing a dewatering action to mitigate the impact until the tank battery can be moved, as the tanks are currently frozen to the ground. The timeframe for moving the tanks to delineate the affected area appears to be over the weekend. While onsite, crews were attempting to locate any tears in containment, which was being hampered by the icy buildup inside the containment. Workers were also mobilizing tankers to dewater the area and tanks in the tank battery in preparation for movement off containment to allow resource to delineate the affected area. The affected area seems to stop about 10' from the berm, according to test pits dug for assessment. The spill will be going to Act 2. SWN Representative Mike Deming said a possible change in protocol from a 6" to a 12" tank freeboard is being considered. Violations are attached.

Comments: On October 5, 2020, I conducted a follow up inspection of the Fred Jones Well Site in Independence Township, Washington County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the Department on 10/4/2020 (CID#352896) . The 10/4/2020 report indicated that approximately 630 gallons of brine was spilled to the well pad. I spoke with Operator representative Casey Barkus on 10/5/2020. Mr. Barkus indicated that a non-structural weld developed a pin hole in the brine tank and caused a stream of brine to shoot across the well pad. Mr. Barkus indicated that the release continued until the brine could be removed from the brine tank. Mr. Barkus indicated that the brine was contained on the well pad and that the pad drain valves were closed. Mr. Barkus indicated that the operator would be utilizing Act 2 clean up as a remediation standard.At the time of inspection, I spoke with operator Josh Boyda. The operator was utilizing third party contractors Miller Environmental and Moody and Associates to guide the remediation of the impacted area. The operator was utilizing a skid steer and excavator to removed impacted material. Mr. Boyda indicated that the impacted material has been placed in the roll off boxes and the crew is awaiting additional disposal boxes to be delivered. I observed 5 rolloff boxes staged within secondary containment and 2 more rolloff boxes located near the impacted area. Mr. Boyda indicated that approximately 12 yards of impacted material has been placed in each rolloff box. The impacted area appeared to be 100' x 60' area located between the brine tank battery and the fenced in well head area. Approximately 6” of material had been removed from the impacted area. Mr. Boyda showed me the non-structural weld on the brine tank that caused the release. The weld in question is located on the brine tank approximately 6' from the bottom of tank on the left side of the brine tank manufacturer information plate.I utilized a Spectrum Field Scout Direct Soil EC meter to screen for conductivity. I screened the impacted area, outlet location and the standing water within the pad drain system.At the impacted area near the fenced well head the meter indicated conductivity of 8.75 mS/cm.At the approximately center of the impacted area of the well pad the meter indicated conductivity of 12.80 mS/cm.At the storm water inlet in the northwest corner of the well pad the meter indicated that conductivity was Or (Or is over range. The meter's max conductivity limit is 20 mS/cm).At the outlet of the pad drain on the meter indicated that conductivity was 0.5 mS/cm.The pad drain outlet appeared to be closed. I recommend that the Operator removed the standing fluid from the outlet and keep the pad drain valve close until remediation is finished and verified.The operator is in compliance with the Department spill policy for reporting and remediation of spills greater than 42 gallons.Violations are being issued for the failure to control a regulated fluid resulting in a release to the ground.The Department requests clarification of how the Operator calculated the amount of fluid released.

The operator was utilizing a skid steer and excavator to removed impacted material. Mr. Boyda indicated that the impacted material has been placed in the roll off boxes and the crew is awaiting additional disposal boxes to be delivered. I observed 5 rolloff boxes staged within secondary containment and 2 more rolloff boxes located near the impacted area. Mr. Boyda indicated that approximately 12 yards of impacted material has been placed in each rolloff box. The impacted area appeared to be 100' x 60' area located between the brine tank battery and the fenced in well head area. Approximately 6” of material had been removed from the impacted area. Mr. Boyda showed me the non-structural weld on the brine tank that caused the release. The weld in question is located on the brine tank approximately 6' from the bottom of tank on the left side of the brine tank manufacturer information plate.I utilized a Spectrum Field Scout Direct Soil EC meter to screen for conductivity. I screened the impacted area, outlet location and the standing water within the pad drain system.At the impacted area near the fenced well head the meter indicated conductivity of 8.75 mS/cm.At the approximately center of the impacted area of the well pad the meter indicated conductivity of 12.80 mS/cm.At the storm water inlet in the northwest corner of the well pad the meter indicated that conductivity was Or (Or is over range. The meter's max conductivity limit is 20 mS/cm).At the outlet of the pad drain on the meter indicated that conductivity was 0.5 mS/cm.The pad drain outlet appeared to be closed. I recommend that the Operator removed the standing fluid from the outlet and keep the pad drain valve close until remediation is finished and verified.The operator is in compliance with the Department spill policy for reporting and remediation of spills greater than 42 gallons.Violations are being issued for the failure to control a regulated fluid resulting in a release to the ground.The Department requests clarification of how the Operator calculated the amount of fluid released.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Rockdale Marcellus Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-09-03
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 860694
Permit API: 117-22060
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Union Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 2019-09-03
Comments: Results from sample IDs 0718-101, 0718-102, and 0718-103, collected 8/19/2019 as documented in inspection report number 2922630, were received from the laboratory on 8/31/2019. At the time of inspection, a large volume of fluid was observed in the northeast corner of the pad surface and was discharging into the rock-lined stormwater channel, which begins at this corner of the pad, and flowing into the northeast infiltration basin. Conductivity of the fluid on the pad surface in the northeast corner of the pad had electrical conductivity (EC) readings between 4.61 mS/cm and 7.19 mS/cm. In the basin, the fluid entering from the channel had an EC of 5.85 mS/cm. Elevated levels of barium, strontium, and chlorides in samples 0718-101 and 0718-102, collected from the pad surface and the northeast infiltration basin, respectively, indicate that a discharge of a pollutional substance occurred. The discharge of a pollutional substance to the infiltration basin, considered Waters of the Commonwealth, is a violation of Section 401 of the Clean Streams Law. The volume of the release is underdetermined. The Department recommends following the process outlined in 78a66 in order to remediate the release. Violations noted. The violation cited on 8/26/2019 (IR #2925622) remains outstanding.

SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/17/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 8211457
Permit API: 047-24792
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/17/2024
Comments: This inspection occurred in response to a phone called made by Jeff Passarello, of Seneca Resources, to Brian Ayers, WQS Supervisor with the Department, on December 16, 2024. The purpose of the phone call was to report an incident which had occurred on Clermont Pad D. It was reported that approximately a total of 10 barrels of production fluid was released from a pipeline while doing maintenance on a pump. The pump was in secondary containment at the time of the incident. The system which controlled the flow of production fluid had not been turned off before performing maintenance on the pump. As a result, production fluid projected out of the pipeline. It is estimated that approximately 5 barrels of production fluid remained in secondary containment and approximately 5 barrels of production fluid discharged onto the well pad outside of the secondary containment. Upon arrival to the site, it was noted that the pump had been removed and placed on the pad away from where the spill occurred. The system controlling the flow of production fluid had been turned off, resolving the source of where the spill had originated. An excavator was used to remove contaminated material from the well pad. Four dumpsters were on site which contained the contaminated waste from the incident. The released production fluid appeared to be primarily within 10 yards of where the incident occurred and remained on the pad. There was no evidence of any production fluid off the well site.Confirmatory field sampling will occur to confirm full remediation of the site. Follow up inspections will be performed routinely until the cleanup is deemed complete.

Comments: The operator submitted a Notice of Intent and Alternate Method of Plugging to the Department for the Thunder Unit One 1V gas well. The Department reviewed the well record and related information and determined that the well was not drilled and cased in conformance with casing and cementing requirements in the 2012 Oil and Gas Act (58 Pa. C.S. §§ 3201-3274) and 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78. The operator failed to segregate and protect the workable Pittsburgh coal seam by setting and cementing a coal protective casing across the workable Pittsburgh coal seam. The operator failed to drill approximately 50 feet below the Deepest Fresh Groundwater (DFGW) and permanently cement a surface casing at that depth. DFGW was identified on the well record at 780 feet. 13 3/8" surface casing was set and cemented at 284 feet. Quarterly Mechanical Integrity Assessment data (MIA) and regulatory Inactive well annual mechanical integrity data was not submitted to the Department for the following inspection years. 2020, 2019, 2018, 2017, 2016, 2014, and 2013. The Thunder Unit One 1V was on inactive status from 9/10/2013-9/10/2018.

Comments: On 6/23/2026, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an admin inspection for the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection is to report the results of four liquid samples that were collected during fracking operations from four locations at the site. During inspection #4183490 conducted on 4/21/2024, the department discovered instances of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad surface, in the sediment basin below the north side of the pad and in liquid flowing past the LOD. Samples were collected from four locations. On 6/18/2024, the department received the results of the samples. Liquid in a 3' x 1.5' x 5" deep puddle, above the center outfall on the north side of the pad, field tested at 9.40 mS conductance. Sample 9551-242 was collected from the puddle. Reference pictures 1, 2, and 3.Liquid flowing into the southeast corner of the sediment basin from the rock lined outfall from the pad field tested at 10.30 mS conductance. Sample 9551-243 was collected from the flowing liquid. Reference pictures 4, 5, and 6.Liquid in the sediment pond next to the east overflow field tested at 3.04 mS conductance. Sample 9551-244 was collected from the pond. Reference pictures 7, 8, and 9.Liquid flowing north from the sediment basin, past the last compost filter sock and past the LOD field tested at 3.33 mS conductance. Sample 9551-245 was collected from the flowing liquid. Reference pictures 10, 11, and 12.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations. The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth.

Violations remain outstanding for 12/19/22 produced fluid release to Pad B.
